agree.label: Agree to help
agree.consequence: “Thanks. I’ll be right back.” You stay by the door, still unsure what Jun wanted you to look out for.

decline.label: Decline politely
decline.consequence: “No worries,” Jun says. You step aside, and Jun goes to ask the cashier for help.

accuse.label: Accuse Jun publicly
accuse.consequence: Jun steps away as shoppers turn to look. The cashier asks everyone to give Jun some space. The accusation leaves Jun upset, and what happened is still unclear.

items.statement: A gap is visible in a row of identical snack packets.
items.feedback: The gap is visible in the display. It does not explain where a packet went.

items.statement: A gap means someone took a packet without paying.
items.feedback: The clue leaves this unknown: Who moved a packet, or when the space appeared.

items.statement: The packet belongs to the person standing nearest to it.
items.feedback: The clue leaves this unknown: Who put it there or whether it has been paid for.

items.statement: A sealed snack packet is sitting on a small display table.
items.feedback: The packet and its location are visible. Payment and ownership are still unknown.

items.statement: A tote bag is resting next to the display table.
items.feedback: You can see the tote beside the table. Its contents and purpose are unknown.

items.statement: The bag was placed there to hide something.
items.feedback: The clue leaves this unknown: Who owns the bag or what is inside it.

items.statement: Every transaction would be visible from the aisle.
items.feedback: The clue leaves this unknown: Which items have been paid for.

items.statement: The cashier is working at a counter with a register and a receipt tray.
items.feedback: The cashier, register and receipt tray are visible. Those details cannot verify a particular sale.

items.statement: The entrance is open and has a green welcome mat.
items.feedback: The open entry and the green mat are visible. They do not reveal who passed through.

items.statement: A request to watch the door means a theft is planned.
items.feedback: The clue leaves this unknown: Who has recently entered or left.

items.question: Jun asks you to watch the door. How do you respond?

A.feedback: Agreeing makes you part of a request you are unsure about.

B.text: I don’t want to do that. Let’s just shop normally.
B.feedback: This response sets a clear boundary and refuses the request calmly.

C.text: Fine, but only for a minute.
C.feedback: A time limit still means agreeing to take part.

D.text: You’re definitely stealing! I’m telling everyone!
D.feedback: A public accusation escalates the situation. Jun’s intentions remain unknown.

items.title: Part A · Pressure tactic
items.question: What is Jun doing to influence your decision?

options.A: Appealing to your friendship to encourage you to comply.
options.B: Giving you a neutral explanation of store rules.
options.C: Asking you to compare product prices.
options.D: Providing verified evidence that no wrongdoing is involved.

items.explanation: “We’re friends right?” appeals to your friendship. It can make agreeing feel like a way to prove your loyalty.

items.title: Part B · Requested role
items.question: What is Jun asking you to do?

options.B: Watch the shop entrance and alert Jun if someone approaches.
options.D: Check the price of a snack.

items.explanation: A lookout watches the entrance and alerts someone when another person approaches. That describes the role Jun is asking you to take.

decisions.label: Decision A
decisions.text: Agree to watch the entrance for Jun.

decisions.label: Decision C
decisions.text: Publicly accuse Jun of stealing without evidence.

immediate.lookOut: You take on the lookout role without knowing Jun’s intentions.
immediate.avoidInvolvement: You avoid participating in the unexplained lookout request.

later.maintainBoundary: You maintain your personal boundary, although Jun might be disappointed.
later.damageTrust: An unsupported accusation could unfairly damage Jun’s reputation or relationships.
later.possibleProblems: If wrongdoing occurs, your involvement could create problems for you and others.

items.title: Acknowledge the friendship or situation

fragments.text: I know we’re friends, and I want to help you.
Everyone should know what you’re doing.

items.feedback: Acknowledge the friendship so the conversation can stay respectful.

items.title: Suggest a constructive alternative

fragments.text: Let’s just shop normally and pay for what we want.
Just make sure nobody catches you.

items.feedback: Suggest a responsible alternative that gives Jun another way forward.

items.title: Encourage a positive next action

fragments.text: Come on, we can head to the counter together.
I’ll tell everyone you’re a thief.
You should never speak to me again.

items.feedback: Offer a specific, positive step that you can take together.

items.title: Who to approach
items.question: Who would be appropriate to approach?

options.text: The shop cashier or a trusted adult.
A group of friends who can confront Jun.

items.feedback: Shop staff or a trusted adult can listen privately and decide how to respond to what you observed.

items.title: What to communicate
items.question: What should you communicate?

options.text: Jun asked me to watch the entrance, but I don’t know why.
Everyone should stay away from Jun.

items.feedback: Describe the request you heard and say what you are unsure about. The request alone leaves Jun’s intentions unknown.

items.title: Safe next action
items.question: What should you do after seeking help?

options.text: Allow the responsible adult or shop staff to assess the situation, while staying safe.
Follow Jun and secretly record him for social media.
Publicly confront Jun and demand an explanation.

items.feedback: Give the adult or staff member space to assess the situation. Stay somewhere safe and let them handle the follow-up.

evidenceCards.text: The visitor must have stolen the compass.
A record authorises moving the compass to the seasonal display.
These records do not establish that the visitor stole anything. The authorised move is a reason to check the display.
An observer recorded a visitor with a tote near the entrance.
Buying display labels proves the label buyer took the compass.

letter-opening.name: Letter fragment · Greeting
letter-opening.description: “Dear detective, begin at the study bookshelf. First choose the symbol that grows on a branch.”

letter-middle.name: Letter fragment · Instructions
letter-middle.description: “Next choose the symbol that changes shape in the night sky. Last choose the symbol that opens locks. Read the spine numbers in that order.”

letter-end.name: Letter fragment · Sign-off
letter-end.description: “One last detail for the safe later: the house on the living room painting has exactly two lit windows. Yours, the challenge host.”

letter.name: Reconstructed letter
letter.description: At the study shelf, choose what grows on a branch, what changes shape in the night sky, and what opens locks. Read their spine numbers in that order. For later, remember the two lit windows in the living room painting.

cipher-rubbing.name: Selected spine numbers
cipher-rubbing.description: Leaf: 3. Moon: 7. Key: 4. Read those numbers in the letter’s order to open the desk drawer.

incident-report.name: Incident report
incident-report.description: Training case SQ-01. A boxed compass was reported missing from its usual shelf. Its absence was confirmed. The report names no suspect and records no removal.

witness-note.name: Witness note · 14:16
witness-note.description: 14:16 — The witness told the clerk the compass shelf was empty. “I had seen a visitor by the entrance. They must have taken it,” the witness added. This last sentence is their interpretation.

partial-reference.name: Partial evidence reference
partial-reference.description: Case SQ-01 needs the receipt, clock observation, witness note, and transaction record. Put the events in time order at the study timeline to recover the full reference.

shop-receipt.name: Shop receipt · 14:05
shop-receipt.description: 14:05 — The register printed a receipt for a roll of display labels. The receipt lists labels only. It records no purchase of the compass.

clock-observation.name: Clock observation · 14:11
clock-observation.description: 14:11 — A training observer recorded a visitor with a canvas tote by the entrance. The observer did not see the visitor handle the compass.

transaction-record.name: Transaction record · 14:22
transaction-record.description: 14:22 — The clerk retrieved a stock-transfer record authorising the boxed compass to move to the seasonal display. The clerk had yet to verify its location.

timeline-reference.name: Evidence reference SQ-01
timeline-reference.description: Chronology verified. Review the sources on the evidence board. For later, retain the minute shown on the third event’s document.

safe-instructions.name: Safe code worksheet
safe-instructions.description: The worksheet lists the four digits in order. Open the Study Safe to see them above the keypad.

house-key.name: House Exit Key
house-key.description: The supervised challenge key. Use it at the front door to finish the level.

final-evidence.name: Final evidence file
final-evidence.description: A stock check found the boxed compass on the seasonal display, as the authorised transfer recorded. The visitor’s presence by the entrance never established that they took it. Report what the sources show and name what remains uncertain.

letter.title: The Torn Letter
hints: Search the living room furniture and wall art.
Look for the greeting, the unfinished instructions, and the host’s sign-off.
Start with “Dear detective”, follow with “Next choose”, and end with “One last detail” and the signature.

cipher.title: The Bookshelf Cipher
hints: Read the reconstructed letter in your inventory.
Match each description to a symbol on a spine. A changing shape at night points to the Moon.
Choose Leaf, then Moon, then Key. Read those spine digits left to right for the drawer.

timeline.title: The Incident Timeline
hints: Check the study drawer, filing cabinet, kitchen cabinet, and wall clock.
Match each event to the time its source actually records. Use the time the clerk retrieved the record, rather than the time a stock move might have happened.
Order the receipt printout, visitor observation, empty-shelf report, and stock-record retrieval from earliest to latest.

board.title: The Evidence Board
hints: Read the three sections on the board.
The records give you two verified observations.
Select Finish Evidence Review to get the safe code worksheet.

study-safe.title: The Final Safe
hints: Read the safe code worksheet and reopen the earlier puzzle rewards.
The four digits come from the painting detail in the letter, one spine, one minute digit, and a count of observation cards.
Use two lit windows, the Moon’s spine number, the ones digit of the witness note’s minute, and the two verified observations.

safeDigits.clue: Last digit of the third event’s time (14:16)
